title: Set the right Multitap port for a four-player PS2 game
summary: Map a four-player PS2 session by checking which console port the game expects, assigning emulator slots in order, and testing every seat before loading a long match.
heroAlt: A Sony PlayStation 2 Multitap adapter with four controller sockets.
author: EmuCore - Hub

blocks.text: Why the port choice changes who can join

A PS2 Multitap expands one physical controller port into slots A through D. PCSX2 accepts those extra controller inputs, but its documentation says memory cards used with a Multitap are not supported. Games may require the Multitap on port 1 or port 2 and can expect a particular slot order. Check the game manual or its multiplayer screen; enabling both ports without evidence can make diagnosis harder.

Use a game you own and a local mode that accepts several players. Close the game before changing controller topology so the next boot reads one stable configuration. Record the current settings for both ports, which device belongs to each player, and any title-specific input profile. This lets you restore the two-player baseline if the game ignores extra seats.

items: 1. Open Settings > Controllers and locate the Multitap option for each port.
2. Check the game manual or multiplayer setup screen for the required port; enable the Multitap on that port only.
3. Assign the first device to slot A, then map additional players to B, C, and D in the displayed order.
4. Leave the other port unchanged unless the game explicitly asks for a second Multitap.
5. Cold-boot the game, open its local-player screen, and join one player at a time.
6. Confirm each seat responds to a different device before starting a match.

blocks.text: A useful test shows four distinct player indicators responding independently. Press one harmless menu direction on each controller in turn and confirm only its intended seat reacts. Back out without saving if the game has no safe test lobby. Record the required port and slot order with the title profile so reconnecting devices does not silently change player assignments.

items: Only two players appear: confirm local four-player support and the port named in the game manual.
Two seats move together: one host input is bound to both; clear only the duplicate binding and retest.
The game detects a Multitap but no extra players: check slot order and cold-boot after changing topology.
Memory-card saves vanish with a Multitap enabled: PCSX2 documents no Multitapped-card support; use a normal card setup to save.

blocks.text: Close emulation, disable the Multitap you added, and restore the recorded port and profile assignments. Reopen the title and verify players 1 and 2 still work. Do not delete or format a memory card to troubleshoot controller topology; input slots and save storage are separate settings.
